answer: Each identity claims one timber yard slot and locks a 70-credit bond. It files a kernel record for its lot and load, then posts a yard signal reading. A yard auditor recomputes the load from the kernel record and signal, burning the bond on any mismatch. The kth slot costs 50+14(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 7,043,000 in fees plus 70,000 in bonds, since neither slot nor sensor can be shared. A rented-signal ring fails: a reused signal under another key is caught on reweighing and both bonds burn. An honest operator pays 50 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
